definitions.explanation: Classical auxiliary expressing strong obligation, appropriateness, or natural expectation. Attaches to the dictionary form of a verb. Found in formal maxims, notices, classical literature, and stiff written prose.

examples.japanese: ⟦{立|た}ち{入|い}る→立ち入る：26367_tachiiru⟧べからず。
examples.english: No entry. (Literally: One must not enter.)
examples.notes: べからず is the negative form of べし: "must not"

examples.japanese: {為政者|いせいしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{民|たみ}→民：13246_tami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{耳|みみ}を{傾|かたむ}ける→耳を傾ける：06903_mimiwokatamukeru⟧べし。
examples.english: Those who govern should listen to the voice of the people.

examples.japanese: ⟦{武士|ぶし}→武士：03989_bushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{名誉|めいよ}→名誉：10568_meiyo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{重|おも}んずる→重んじる：14445_omonjiru⟧べし⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われていた→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It was said that a samurai should value honor.

notes:
Archaic/formal auxiliary. In modern Japanese, べし has largely been replaced by べき (attributive) and should/must expressions using ⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧ or ～すべき.

FORMS:
- べし (predicative): 行くべし (one should go)
- べき (attributive): 行くべき⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧ (the path one should take)
- べく (conjunctive): 行くべく (in order to go; so as to go)
- べからず (negative): 行くべからず (one must not go)

The negative べからず still appears commonly on formal notices and signs.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- べき: should; ought to (the attributive form, widely used in modern Japanese)
- べく: in order to (conjunctive form, used in formal writing)
